subject: Tick format for log scales in git head

messages.author: f1c69ac31c9b9115
messages.subject: Tick format for log scales in git head
parts:
Hello,

Using the version of ggplot2 from github (installed using the excellent install_github method from devtools) I am having some trouble with the tick mark formatting of log scales.  Previously it was of the form 10^x where x was suitably raised.  However, in the current version it is using scientific notation of the form 1e+01.  This is both an eyesore and consumes a lot of horizontal space on the plot.

Is this a bug, or just a new default?  And, if it is not a bug, how can I revert back to the 10^x format I am used to?

Regards, Freddie.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Tick format for log scales in git head
parts:
It's a bit more complicated now. You can do it by using scale_y_log10, or by doing the log transform yourself. These two  examples below will give the same output:

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
ggplot(pressure, aes(x=temperature, y=pressure)) + geom_point() +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x), 
                labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))) +
                  
ggplot(pressure, aes(x=temperature, y=log10(pressure))) + geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "pressure", labels = math_format(10^.x))

-Winston
